Hi Grace and Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed. We want to lock a small dedicated fleet for our pilot (3 x A100-equivalent slots, estimated sustained 40 qps) for the month of August, with a potential scale to 12 slots if performance/usage proves out in month two. Procurement asked for a short note on timing and whether Redwood can guarantee burst capacity during our ramp.

I attached the high-level MOPA/throughput PDF and added a CSV export of our forecast. Can you confirm by EOD Tuesday if you can reserve the baseline slots and what the cost/runway looks like?

Sophie
Skyscale.ai

Attachment: skyscale_mopa_requirements.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)
Attachment: Q2_pipeline_snapshot.csv (CSV, 22KB)

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Slot ask for pilot + expected go-live window

Hi Sophie — appreciate the forecast and the clear ask. Looping in Ben (sales finance), Laura (revenue ops) and Jonas (infra/fleet) to lock down the runway and confirm reservation mechanics.

Short answers up front:
- We can commit 3 baseline A100-equivalent slots for Aug 1–31 under a short-term reserved block; pricing and commitment details below will need procurement sign-off.
- Burst to 12 slots is feasible but will require a quick approval from finance + a reserve booking in our Dedicated pool to guarantee latency SLAs; otherwise we provide best-effort burst.

Action items I propose for this week: 
1) Ben — can you run a quick cost/runway delta for baseline vs. burst (include estimated token run-rate impact) and reply with a one-slide summary?
2) Jonas — can infra hold a soft reservation for the 3 baseline slots (no charge) for 48 hours while procurement confirms? If not, outline the exact lead times and fallback (best-effort burst window).
3) Laura — any blockers from revenue ops/contracting if procurement requests a 30-day pilot short-form PO?

I’ve included the attachments from Sophie in the thread for context.

Thanks — Grace
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Grace — attached is a two-row summary I put together for procurement: baseline (3 slots) and ramp (12 slots). Key points:
- Baseline (3 slots, 4 weeks): estimated $18k (tokens + reserved slot surcharge) — supports expected 40 qps sustained for pilot.
- Ramp (12 slots): if we reserve now, monthly commitment ~$62k; if burst on demand, expected higher per-token costs and no latency SLA.
- Net cashflow impact for Redwood: baseline is neutral within Q2 credits; ramp requires a short approval given our capacity commit guidelines.

Ask: Laura — if procurement can sign a 30-day PO for baseline by Thu EOD, we can convert the soft hold to a formal reservation. Jonas — please confirm if infra can convert soft hold to charged reserve once PO is in.

Attachment: RDW-deal-runway-summary-5421.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Confirmed — infra can place a soft, non-billing reservation for 72 hours starting today. If procurement delivers a PO within that window, we will convert to a formal reserved capacity with the pricing Ben outlined. Notes:
- Lead time to guarantee sustained 12-slot capacity (with latency SLA) is ~10 business days if we need to re-balance pools; best-effort burst remains available sooner but without SLA.
- If procurement needs an earlier go-live, we can provide a temporary hybrid: 3 reserved slots + 9 on-demand burst for first two weeks.

Next steps:
- Grace: share the one-slide cost summary to Skyscale procurement and ask for PO by Thu EOD (Ben offering to own this).
- Ben: if PO comes in, please send copy to infra-ops@redwood.com and revenueops@redwood.com so we can trigger conversion.
- Laura: please confirm any contracting approvals needed for a 30-day short-form PO.

Jonas
